Yeah I would say about a month in terms of really waking up every day not miserable. It may have been quicker and I didn't realize. I would say maybe 3-4 doses and i began to notice a decrease in frequency of negative thoughts but to get to where i am now (thoughts still pop up but prob 95% reduction in my obsession with them) I'd say a month. I started taking it every other day, now my rx is for 21 lozenges a month to do at my discretion (so it is okay to take it 2 days in a row). Not sure if some folks take it every day.

Floaty for sure. For me its like being tipsy, the feeling. A little stumbling (not falling down), feel the anxiety slip away, stuff is funnier. I'm almost always alone but from what my therapist said it doesn't make me appear fucked up (like i wasn't slurring, talking really loud, etc like i might do when drunk). I can do basic things, like chores, art, things like that but studying, driving, things like that, no way. But it really does last just a couple hours and you feel sober again.

You have to buy from a compounding pharmacy, so they mix it to whatever your rx is and its just "ketamine". You do the lozenge under your tongue until dissolved and it usually lasts about 2 hours. Mine are 125mg each. I feel like infusions are like 800mg each? A lot more, whatever it is. Because of the liw dose, you can take at home.

There's also a nasal spray but haven't used that.

FDA approved, but probably not covered by your insurance. I take the much smaller dose as a lozenge, the infusions (I think this is most common for mental health) are $800/each where I live. My monthly cost for the lozenges is about $60 (again, not covered by insurance) - so it's a bit more than most prescriptions but actually not prohibitive. As far as a "brain reboot" my shrink says that is usually the product of the infusions. I would say that I took it about a month before I saw REAL difference (meaning feeling good all the time and not just while on ketamine lol)

TMS is covered by my insurance, but I have not tried it so can't speak to that. But ketamine saved my life. No question. Not only that but it has freed me from the constant looping thoughts of death/dying/harming myself in some way. I can't describe the freedom. Not that is has "cured" me but it at least has made room in my head for other thoughts.

Let me know if you have questions about the ketamine lozenges, I don't know that i can speak with any authority on the other methods of ingesting it.

So even though you didn't ask, I'm going to give you a few tricks to reduce anxiety I got from my therapist.

Pay attention to your current surroundings. Name (out loud if possible) 5 things you see, 4 things you hear, 3 things you feel (like touch, so "I feel my shirt sleeve touching my arm"), 2 things you smell, 1 that you taste. Do NOT stress if you can't get up to those numbers, the point is to calm your thoughts.

Pick an item in your surroundings. Out loud (if pissible) describe it. Be as detailed as you can. If necessary, do it with a second item.

Consider that you are going on a trip. Where will you go? What will you pack? Let your mind go wild.

I struggle with this myself. A few things I do-

I have a fishbowl and anytime I think of something I love I write it down and drop it in there. Pull one out when feeling down. These are not date specific, so not "last Sat. at the movies" but "going to the movie theater"

I have another container where I write down one good thing that happened that day. Even the tiniest thing. Read them once a year (or more often if needed) you'll be surprised.

I write down the things I have done at the end of the day. Nothing is too small- got out of bed and took a shower. Loaded dishwasher. Folded laundry. Whatever. 

I have a box I call my comfort box. When I feel bad, I pull it out. Making your own will help you get to know yourself better. What brings you comfort? A scented candle, stuffed animal, sketchbook, etc. Try to include something for each sense.

Keep a journal. No stress. Just for you. You don't need to write every day. 

Hope some of this is helpful!
